summary: Frontend-only smoke test after the React 19 -> 18.3.1 downgrade. Found a HARD CRASH: react-leaflet@5.0.0 requires React ^19 (it renders <Context> directly as a provider), so on React 18 the customer home page (/app) threw 'TypeError: render is not a function' inside MapContainerComponent and the whole CustomerHome tree unmounted (stations-map, wallet-card, repair-charger-btn, station-code-input all gone). I applied the in-scope dependency fix: yarn add react-leaflet@4.2.1 (React 18 peer; +@react-leaflet/core@2.1.0) and restarted frontend. After the fix everything is green: customer/owner/admin logins land on the right dashboards, map renders 9 markers + popups + 'Start charging' deep link, full charging flow (IND000001 -> charger-detail -> start -> live ring 20%->24% -> stop-confirm -> billed ₹31.89 in history), repairs create (REP-10049) + list + detail, wallet top-up (₹1,234->₹1,334), notifications panel, theme toggle light/dark, mobile 390px drawer. ZERO console/page errors and zero failing /api calls in the post-fix runs.

issues: CARTO basemap tiles (basemaps.cartocdn.com light_all/dark_all) now render a diagonal 'API KEY REQUIRED / carto.com/basemaps#apikey' watermark across every tile in both light and dark mode. Switch to a keyless provider (e.g. https://tile.openstreetmap.org/{z}/{x}/{y}.png) or add a CARTO key via env.

action_items: KEEP/commit the react-leaflet@4.2.1 downgrade in package.json + yarn.lock (I applied it) — react-leaflet@5 is incompatible with React 18.3.1 and crashes /app. Alternative: revert React to 19 and instead fix react-day-picker (v9 supports React 19) — but do NOT ship React 18 with react-leaflet 5.
Replace CARTO tile URLs with a keyless tile provider (API KEY REQUIRED watermark visible on the map).

Optional: ChargerPage station title has no data-testid (only charger-detail/charger-status exist); 'charger-name' testid currently belongs to the Admin add-charger form input, which is confusing for tests.
critical_code_review_comments: Dependency compatibility must be checked across the whole tree when pinning React: react-leaflet 5 (peer react ^19) was the only React-19-only package and was missed by the downgrade. Run `yarn install` and check peer-dependency warnings before deploying.
StationsMap.jsx uses only v4-compatible react-leaflet APIs (MapContainer/TileLayer/Marker/Popup), so the 4.2.1 downgrade needed no code change.

rca_of_the_issue: react-leaflet@5.0.0 declares peerDependencies react ^19 and relies on React 19's ability to render a Context object directly as a provider (<Context value=...>). Under React 18 that JSX is treated as a Context.Consumer, whose child must be a function -> 'TypeError: render is not a function' in updateContextConsumer, crashing CustomerHome. Fixed by installing react-leaflet@4.2.1 (peer react ^18) which uses <Context.Provider>; no application code change required.
